newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar may test above 119 yen in Asia before data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar may test above 119 yen in Asia before data.

text.p: The dollar is expected to build a base for a climb above technical resistance at 119 yen in Asia on Friday, but active buying may be limited before the release of several key U.S. economic indicators, including jobs data.

"The technical trend looks very healthy for the dollar after the rally overnight. It should test 119 yen, but I'm not sure whether the market will buy aggressively ahead of the jobs data," a Japanese long-term credit bank dealer said.
Dealers said dollar offers are seen lined up before the resistance point, but a clear break could speed up the buying, with stop-loss buy orders rumoured at about 119.10-15 yen.
"If the dollar manages to hit the stop-loss orders then it may rise towards 119.50 yen," the dealer said.
Dealers said the dollar was expected to be supported on demand from Japanese investors and short-covering interest should it dip towards 118 yen.
The dollar got a boost in New York overnight from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin who reiterated his support for a strong dollar, which helps keep inflation low.
"We have always said we believe a strong dollar is in our interest," Rubin told Reuters in an interview while adding it was unclear whether demand in Japan was helping the expansion.
